# Spec: tunez (fixture — success criteria from the tunez run, run paths replaced)

## Success criteria

- **S1 — Pitch detection accuracy**: The pitch detector meets fixed accuracy thresholds on synthetic and real singing.
  - Current: no detector exists.
  - Target: on synthetic voice-like harmonic tones across E2–C6 (with and without ±50¢ vibrato and −20 dB white noise), ≥ 99% of voiced frames estimate f0 within ±5¢ and 0 frames are octave errors; on the Vocadito dataset (CC BY 4.0; a subset committed under `test/fixtures/vocadito/` with its licence and citation), raw pitch accuracy — mir_eval semantics: the detector's best-guess pitch (reported even on frames it gates as unvoiced) within ±50¢ of the reference on reference-voiced frames, estimates resampled to reference timestamps — is ≥ 90%, and octave errors (estimate within ±50¢ of 2× or 0.5× the reference) are ≤ 3% of reference-voiced frames. The range edges E2 and C6 are in the sweep; input below E2 or above C6 is reported as out of range, not as a wrong note; on silence and on noise alone ≥ 99% of frames are reported unvoiced; synthetic metrics are measured at both 44.1 kHz and 48 kHz sample rates; all synthetic signals are seeded so re-runs give identical metrics. Cents are relative to A4 = 440 Hz.
  - Acceptance: `npm run test:accuracy` exits 0 and writes `reports/accuracy.json` containing the four metrics, each meeting its threshold.
- **S2 — Key-aware target inference**: The inferred target note matches the note the singer is aiming for, including when they are far off.
  - Current: none.
  - Target: on a seeded synthetic melody corpus of ≥ 240 melodies (all 24 keys, diatonic melodies with vibrato, per-note bias, onset scoops, and ≥ 20% of notes sung 50–80¢ off toward an out-of-key neighbour): (a) after the key is locked, the target equals the ground-truth intended note on ≥ 97% of voiced frames outside each note's onset trim (its first 120 ms; corpus scoops are capped at ≤ 80¢ deep and ≤ 60 ms long); (b) on the 50–80¢-off notes, key-aware targeting picks the intended in-key note on ≥ 90% of frames, and the report includes the chromatic-only baseline for comparison; (c) the target is never an octave away from the intended note; (d) the detected key's pitch-class set matches ground truth within 10 s of voiced singing on ≥ 90% of melodies; (e) before key confidence is reached, the inference layer (before display hysteresis) selects the nearest chromatic note; (f) with no voiced input, no target is shown and the key reads as still being detected.
  - Acceptance: `npm run test:accuracy` exits 0 and `reports/accuracy.json` contains metrics (a)–(d) meeting thresholds; unit tests assert (e) and (f).
- **S3 — Stable display (no jitter)**: Held notes produce a steady target and steady in-tune state.
  - Current: none.
  - Target: driving the display pipeline with a 3 s held note centred on the target with ±30¢ vibrato at 5.5 Hz at the ±20¢ preset: the displayed target changes 0 times and the in-tune state is "in tune" on ≥ 95% of frames after the first 300 ms; a pitch hovering at a semitone boundary (±10¢ noise around 50¢) changes the displayed target at most once per 250 ms (the anti-jitter mechanism is a cents hysteresis band of about 15¢, bypassed on jumps over one semitone — not a time dwell); when voicing stops, the display shows the no-pitch state ("Listening…", note and cents cleared) within 250 ms plus one display frame, and no stale target after that.
  - Acceptance: a deterministic unit test of the display pipeline (`npm test`) asserts each number above.
- **S4 — Latency ≤ 100 ms**: Feedback appears within 100 ms of the sound that caused it.
  - Current: none.
  - Target: the pipeline's algorithmic delay (analysis window + hop + smoothing group delay) is ≤ 70 ms; in Chromium with a fake microphone fed a stepped-pitch file, the in-app latency probe measures, on the pitch-gauge needle (which redraws every display frame), p95 (frame render time − capture time of the audio frame it reflects) ≤ 100 ms over a 20 s run; the note name, cents number and state pill update at most 10 times per second by design, with ≥ 100 measured samples (a run with fewer fails rather than passing vacuously).
  - Acceptance: a unit test asserts the algorithmic delay ≤ 70 ms; the e2e latency test (`npm run test:e2e`) writes `reports/latency.json` with p95 ≤ 100 and sample count ≥ 100.
- **S5 — Tolerance presets**: Three presets, ±35¢, ±20¢ and ±10¢, control the in-tune judgement everywhere.
  - Current: none.
  - Target: the user selects one of three presets on the Sing screen (before a song) or as the default in Settings; the Settings default persists across reloads and applies each time the app opens; the Sing-screen control is disabled from Start until the song ends, and a change made there applies to the next song only; live view, report and exercise scoring all use the active preset; |deviation| equal to the tolerance counts as in tune; with nothing saved (first run) the preset is ±20¢; the report is computed at the song's preset and names it; cents are displayed as signed integers (e.g. +12¢, −8¢) while judgement uses the unrounded value.
  - Acceptance: unit tests assert in-tune results at deviations 9/10/11¢, 19/20/21¢ and 34/35/36¢ for the matching presets; an e2e test sets each Settings default, reloads, and finds it selected on Sing; another finds the Sing control disabled during a song.
- **S6 — Key control**: Key is automatic by default and can be locked manually.
  - Current: none.
  - Target: the live screen shows the current key and whether it is auto-detected (with a confidence indication), still being detected (chromatic fallback), or locked; the user can lock any of the 24 major/minor keys, which takes effect on the next analysed frame, and unlock back to auto; a lock lasts until the song ends and each new song starts on auto. Note names are spelled with sharps or flats to suit the current key (e.g. B♭ in F major, A♯ in E major; sharps during chromatic fallback).
  - Acceptance: an e2e test locks a key, verifies the target changes on a fed out-of-key-ambiguous pitch, unlocks, and sees auto mode restored; unit tests cover locked-key targeting and key-dependent note spelling.
- **S7 — Session lifecycle and permission states**: Sessions start, stop and fail predictably.
  - Current: none.
  - Target: Start requests the microphone (first time) and begins analysis; Start is disabled while the microphone is starting and while a session runs, so a double tap starts one session; the session ends on Stop (a second Stop tap has no further effect — one report) or after ≥ 8 s of continuous silence, where silence means no voiced frame; a session with < 10 s of voiced singing (a session with no singing at all included) shows a "too short to analyse" message instead of a report; a denied or unavailable microphone shows an explanation screen with per-platform steps to re-enable it and a retry button; on page hide or interruption (call, lock screen, audio-session interruption, mic track ended or muted) the song pauses — timer frozen, microphone tracks stopped, data kept — and "Tap to resume" re-acquires the microphone and continues the same song, while Stop ends it; the microphone track is stopped whenever no session or exercise is running (paused included).
  - Acceptance: e2e tests cover Stop, double Start/Stop taps, silence auto-stop, too-short, permission-denied, pause on `visibilitychange` and resume, and a check that all `MediaStreamTrack`s report `readyState === "ended"` after each session ends.
- **S8 — Post-song report**: The report states where, and by how much, the singer was sharp or flat, and which patterns they showed.
  - Current: none.
  - Target: the report contains (1) overall signed mean deviation in cents and % of voiced time in tune; (2) a per-note table: note name with octave, number of sung notes, signed mean deviation in cents, % in tune; (3) a deviation-over-time chart; (4) six pattern verdicts — overall bias, per-note bias, high vs. low register, drift over the song, note onsets (scooping), upward vs. downward leaps — each either a claim with direction and size in cents, "No consistent tendency" (enough data, no effect), or "Not enough data to tell". A pattern is claimed only when its design minimum is met (`design/HANDOFF.md` §report "Pattern rules": 30 notes, a note sung 8 times, 10 notes per half, 30 s, 30 note starts, 8 leaps each way), its effect meets the research cents floor (≥ 10¢ overall and per-note; ≥ 15¢ register, drift, leaps; ≥ 20¢ scooping) and a test survives family-wise correction (Holm, α = 0.05, across every test in the report); below the minimum → "Not enough data to tell", otherwise → "No consistent tendency". All thresholds live in one config module; meeting a threshold exactly counts as met. The timeline is chronological; cents are signed integers.
  - Acceptance: unit tests feed synthetic sessions that each embed one pattern and assert that pattern is claimed with the embedded direction and a size within ±5¢ of the embedded value; across 100 seeded unbiased sessions, no pattern is claimed in more than 5% of them (they read "No consistent tendency"); a session below each threshold yields "Not enough data to tell" for that pattern; a session exactly at a threshold is evaluated, not abstained.
- **S9 — History and trends**: Reports persist on the device and show cross-session trends.
  - Current: none.
  - Target: every completed song report and exercise result is saved to IndexedDB; a History screen lists them newest first (an empty history shows a "No sessions yet" state) and reopens any one, showing the same numbers as when it was first displayed; if a save fails (e.g. storage quota), the user sees an error and the report is still shown; the user can delete one entry or all (with confirmation); a trends view states cross-session song patterns (the same pattern and direction in ≥ 3 of the last 5 songs; below 5 saved songs: "Not enough sessions yet") only when its threshold is met, otherwise "Not enough sessions yet"; each recurring pattern and the overall bias carry an Improving / Worsening / Steady badge (|now| ≤ |before| − 4¢ / ≥ |before| + 4¢ / otherwise, last 5 songs vs the 5 before; "Not enough data to tell" with fewer than 10 songs); history survives reload and offline use.
  - Acceptance: unit tests on the trends module (claim when met, abstain when not; badge at −4¢/+4¢ boundaries and under 10 songs); e2e test completes two sessions, reloads, sees both in History, deletes one, then deletes all.
- **S10 — Exercises**: Four exercises run end to end and save their results.
  - Current: none.
  - Target: (a) range test records the lowest and highest notes held ≥ 1 s, saves the range, and labels it with the closest voice type; (b) hold-a-note plays a reference tone, then scores the sustained note by signed average deviation (median cents) and wobble (std dev of cents around the singer's own average); (c) scale/arpeggio plays a major or minor scale or arpeggio pattern note by note and scores each sung note; (d) interval matching plays two notes, the user sings them back, and each interval is scored in cents. Reference tones play before the user sings, never during scoring; frames sung while a reference plays are ignored. Range-test holds shorter than 1 s are not counted. If no singing is detected within 3 s after the reference ends (hold-a-note and the drills) or within 8 s in a range-test part, the exercise shows "No singing detected — try again" and saves nothing. Each attempt saves a separate result. Only one song session or exercise can be active at a time. Every exercise defaults to a pitch range inside the saved vocal range (F3–A4 until a range test exists) and lets the user change key/start note before starting.
  - Acceptance: unit tests for each exercise's scoring with synthetic pitch tracks; an e2e test per exercise feeds a fake microphone and finds a result screen with the expected score fields, saved to History.
- **S11 — Installable and offline**: The app installs to the home screen and runs with no network.
  - Current: none.
  - Target: a valid web app manifest (name, icons 192/512 + maskable, `display: standalone`, theme colour) and an Apple touch icon; a service worker precaches every built asset; after one online load, reloading with the network offline renders the app and a session can run.
  - Acceptance: an e2e test loads the app, switches the browser context offline, reloads, starts a session with the fake microphone, and sees live pitch; a test validates the manifest fields. A new deployment's service worker takes over on the next launch without mixing old and new assets.
- **S12 — iOS and Android browser engines**: The full e2e suite passes on both engines at phone size.
  - Current: none.
  - Target: e2e tests run in Playwright's Chromium (Pixel-class viewport) and WebKit (iPhone-class viewport) projects with a simulated microphone available in both engines (an injected test `MediaStream` where the engine has no fake-capture flag); no page has horizontal scroll at 360 and 430 px widths.
  - Acceptance: `npm run test:e2e` exits 0 with both projects executed (the JSON reporter lists tests from both).
- **S13 — Privacy: nothing leaves the device**: No audio or pitch data is transmitted or audio stored.
  - Current: none.
  - Target: during a full session and report, every network request is a same-origin GET for a static asset; no audio samples are written to any storage.
  - Acceptance: an e2e test records all requests during a session + report and asserts each is same-origin GET of a built asset — the full assertion runs in Chromium (service-worker requests observable); in WebKit it runs with service workers blocked for that test so every request reaches the page network; a test inspects IndexedDB records and asserts no audio/PCM fields; `grep` of the built bundle finds no third-party URLs.
- **S14 — Accessible, mobile-first UI**: The UI is usable by touch and readable by everyone.
  - Current: none.
  - Target: in-tune state is conveyed by text or shape as well as colour; text contrast ≥ 4.5:1 (WCAG AA); touch targets ≥ 44×44 CSS px; every control has an accessible name; animation honours `prefers-reduced-motion`.
  - Acceptance: an axe-core scan in the e2e suite reports 0 serious/critical violations on every screen, empty and error states included; a test asserts interactive elements' bounding boxes ≥ 44×44.
- **S15 — Deploy-ready**: The built app is ready for the owner to deploy a Vercel preview by hand after the run (changed mid-run by the owner, 2026-10-07: no deploy during the run).
  - Current: no deployment configuration.
  - Target: `vercel.json` (build command, output directory, framework, headers) and `DEPLOY.md` (the exact preview-deploy commands for project `tunez`, without `--prod`, plus the device checklist for iPhone Safari and Android Chrome) exist; the production build serves `/` and `/manifest.webmanifest` locally; no `vercel` command is run during the build, so no `.vercel/` directory exists.
  - Acceptance: after `npm run build`, `vite preview --port 4173 --strictPort` answers `curl -sI http://localhost:4173/` and `curl -sI http://localhost:4173/manifest.webmanifest` with HTTP 200; `grep -c 'vercel deploy' DEPLOY.md` ≥ 1 and `grep -c -- '--prod' DEPLOY.md` = 0; `test ! -d .vercel` succeeds.
- **S16 — Engineering gate**: Build, typecheck, lint and all tests pass.
  - Current: no project.
  - Target: `npm run build`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint`, `npm test`, `npm run test:accuracy` and `npm run test:e2e` each exit 0 with no new warnings.
  - Acceptance: each command exits 0.

- **S17 — Design: every approved screen is built**: each approved screen in `design/HANDOFF.md` (`live`, `key-picker`, `drone-sheet`, `mic-permission`, `report`, `history`, `trends`, `exercises`, `exercise-setup`, `range-test`, `hold-note`, `scale-drill`, `interval-drill`, `settings`) is marked by a `design: <id>` comment in exactly one source file outside `design/`.
  - Current: the screens exist only as the design package at `design/` (2c3428a).
  - Target: the file that builds each screen carries its `design: <id>` marker.
  - Acceptance: `bash .relay/run/check-design.sh design --verify screens --except .relay/run/SPEC.md` exits 0 (each id marked in exactly one file). Items resolved "spec wins" in `## Design reconciliation` are exempt.
- **S18 — Design: named components exist**: every component in `design/HANDOFF.md` §Components (50 names) exists as an identifier in source outside `design/`.
  - Current: the components are named only in the design package.
  - Target: each has a definition under the name the design uses.
  - Acceptance: `bash .relay/run/check-design.sh design --verify components --except .relay/run/SPEC.md` exits 0 (each name present as a whole word). Items resolved "spec wins" in `## Design reconciliation` are exempt.
- **S19 — Design: tokens live in one theme file**: all 68 tokens in `design/HANDOFF.md` §Design tokens are defined in `src/theme/tokens.ts`, and no token colour value is hard-coded outside it or the files generated from it (index.html, src/theme/tokens.generated.css).
  - Current: the tokens are defined only in the design package.
  - Target: one theme file defines every token; everything else references it, and platform colour values (manifest, theme-color) are generated from it, never duplicated.
  - Acceptance: `bash .relay/run/check-design.sh design --verify tokens --theme src/theme/tokens.ts --allow 'index.html' --allow 'src/theme/tokens.generated.css' --except .relay/run/SPEC.md` exits 0 (names compared case-insensitively with `-`/`_` removed, so `panel-border` matches `panelBorder`; every hex in a value cell is checked, light and dark alike).
- **S20 — Design: copy matches the design**: all 584 strings in `design/HANDOFF.md` §Copy appear verbatim in source outside `design/`.
  - Current: the copy exists only in the design package.
  - Target: the built UI uses the designed wording.
  - Acceptance: `bash .relay/run/check-design.sh design --verify copy --except .relay/run/SPEC.md` exits 0 (each string split on `{name}` placeholders; every fragment of 3+ characters present verbatim, a one-word fragment as a whole word — one-word strings are only presence-checked, so their rendering is left to the post-run screen comparison). Items resolved "spec wins" in `## Design reconciliation` are exempt.
- **S21 — Design: screens captured for review**: for each approved screen, `.relay/run/design-check/<id>.png` exists, or the polish phase's evidence file records `capture unavailable: <id> — <reason>`; the capture code takes its output directory from `RELAY_DESIGN_CHECK_DIR`, so no run path is written into the product.
  - Current: no captures exist.
  - Target: the owner can compare each built screen against `design/screens/<id>.png` after the run; the comparison itself is never a gate.
  - Acceptance: for each id, `test -f .relay/run/design-check/<id>.png` exits 0 or `grep -F 'capture unavailable: <id>' .relay/run/phases/phase-*.evidence.md` prints a line; and `git grep --untracked -lF '.relay/' -- . ':!design' ':!.relay' ':!**/.gitignore'` returns no files.
- **S22 — Reference drone**: The Sing screen can play a reference drone or starting note and warns when the mic hears it.
  - Current: none.
  - Target: the Drone button opens the drone sheet; Drone mode plays a sustained tone at the chosen tonic (default: the locked key, else the detected key at confidence level 2 or above, else none selected and Play disabled), octave 2–5 and volume, continuing after the sheet closes with the button showing "On · {tonic}"; Starting-note mode plays the note for 2 s; the headphones banner shows the first time the drone starts in a session; when the mic hears the drone's pitch class steadily for over 1 s without a voice, the alert banner replaces it, and "Stop drone" stops it; the banner clears after 5 s without the drone.
  - Acceptance: unit tests for tonic defaulting and drone-heard detection (> 1 s steady pitch class, 5 s clear) with synthetic pitch tracks; an e2e test opens the sheet, plays and stops a drone, and checks the button state.


## Assumptions

- none
